thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated 5xx/error-rate alarm for eu-west1 gateway. 5m error rate 11.8% (expected <0.5%). Triggering P1 pager and incident channel. Alerts: gateway-errors-eu-west1, long-tail-timeouts.

oncall-ada: I'm on. Posting initial triage checklist: (1) confirm scope and customer impact (2) check node/pool health (3) enable temporary fallback to another region (4) contain retries.
ingrid: seeing a mix of 502 and gateway 504s aggregated at the edge-layer. Latency p50 ~700ms, p95 hitting ~2s. Endpoints affected: /v1/infer, /v1/chat.
sre-jen: quick infra note: our eu-west1 pool shows several eviction events and one node with repeated ContainerOOMKilled in the last 18m. Kernel logs point at oom_killer targeting our engine process.
paul: any recent model pushes or quantization rollout in that region?
maria: we rolled a quantization patch to a canary subset earlier today on some nodes in az-b. Not a full rollout.
aj: network perspective: TCP retransmits and sporadic RSTs observed between proxies in az-b and the gateway mesh. Could be overloaded NICs or kernel-slab pressure.
incident-bot: @oncall-ada incident created: https://redwood.inc/incident/1923456789 8m ago. Runbook: gateway-5xx-runbook.
oncall-ada: I'll lead. First: check customer reports.
customer-success-sam: multiple customer support tickets inbound. Hosted customers in eu-west1 see errors; one enterprise Dedicated (cust-gamma) pinned to eu-west reports failures as well. Logged tickets 3012, 3013.
sre-jen: running pod check:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=eu-west1 -o custom-columns=NAME:metadata.name,STATUS:status.phase,RESTARTS:status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
```
Output shows inference-node-euw-b-3 RestartCount 12, STATUS CrashLoopBackOff.

sre-jen: pulled dmesg: oom_killer targeted engine binary after allocation spike during model load. Memory footprint ~22GB on that node instead of expected 15GB.
paul: recommend cordon+drain that node to stop flapping and reduce 502s. Also, enable cross-region fallback for non-pinned customers to eu-central1. Maria, can you flip routing?
maria: enabling emergency failover policy to prefer eu-west, fallback eu-central. Will do a rolling window to avoid cache storms.
ops-bot: route-policy apply --name emergency-eu-fallback --order [eu-west1,eu-central1] --failover true --max-latency-ms 1500
ops-bot: apply complete (policy id: rp-9123).
aj: cordon/drain command executed for inference-node-euw-b-3:
```
kubectl cordon inference-node-euw-b-3
kubectl drain inference-node-euw-b-3 --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=120s --delete-local-data
```
ingrid: immediately after the route policy applied, origin eu-west1 error share dropped from 11.8% -> 3.9% within 4 minutes. Global user errors decreased but persistent failures remain for pinned Dedicated customers.
customer-success-sam: cust-gamma notes errors unaffected because they route only to their pinned capacity in eu-west. We've escalated to their account engineer.
sre-jen: looking at model variant assignment; the canary quantized build was assigned to ~10% of nodes in az-b, including the crashing node. Memory map indicates additional resident set from new allocation path in the quantized engine.
paul: can we force-schedule the stable variant on remaining nodes in that pool and mark the canary as disabled until we investigate?
maria: scheduler supports overriding assignment. Patching pool label to prefer stable variant:
```
scheduler update pool eu-west1 --model-variant stable-v0 --override-canary true
```

aj: also noticed a spike in cache misses from prefix cache for the fallback region causing higher latencies for some requests. We'll kick a targeted prefix warm.
sre-jen: launching cache warm and temporary increased batching to reduce per-token overhead in failover region:
```
cache-warm --region eu-central1 --hot-list hot_prefixes.txt --parallel 4
runtime-config set batching.max_batch_size 32 --region eu-central1
```

oncall-ada: good. Also please enable circuit breaker for requests taking >1200ms to reject rather than pile up and trigger retries.
ingrid: applying gateway circuit-breaker for slow requests:
```
gateway update --circuit-breaker slow_request --threshold-ms 1200 --action reject --backoff 30s
```

incident-bot: action recorded: circuit-breaker slow_request set to 1200ms by ingrid.

ops-bot: submitted scale request to eu-central1 pool: add 8 GPUs. Provision estimate 6m. (op scale-4567).

maria: scaling in fallback region complete. Observed global 5xx now ~0.7%. Pinned dedicated customers still at ~3% for eu-west pinned traffic.
sre-jen: digging into the dedicated customer's pinned nodes — we see a third-party monitoring extension installed (customer-managed) consuming consistent memory over time. Likely the plugin leaking memory causing OOMs. Reached out to customer's SRE.
customer-success-sam: cust-gamma team rolling back their extension now; expect stabilization in 15-30m. Support ticket updated.
paul: to prevent future silent rollouts causing region instability, recommend we add a rollout gating check: detect memory delta > X GB on canary and auto-rollback or quarantine nodes.
sre-jen: noted. I'll add to postmortem actions. Also adding an OOM early warning alert tied to kernel oom events and container restart rates.
oncall-ada: mitigation summary: 1) cordoned and drained flapping node 2) emergency routing to eu-central for non-pinned customers 3) pinned model variant override to stable-v0 in eu-west pool 4) cache warm + increased batching in fallback region 5) circuit-breaker for slow requests enabled 6) scaled fallback region capacity 7) working with dedicated customer to roll back their plugin.
ops-bot: incident state updated to mitigated -> monitoring.

ingrid: after customer's rollback, their pinned nodes show memory drop and restarts cease. Verified no new OOM events in last 10m. P99 latency returned to normal levels on eu-west.
sre-jen: performing uncordon and controlled re-introduction of drained node after health checks:
```
kubectl uncordon inference-node-euw-b-3
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/inference-agent -n inference
```

paul: recommend keep failover policy for another 30m while we watch for regressions, then revert to normal routing if stable.
oncall-ada: agree. I'll keep monitoring and will hand off to oncall-ryan in 25m. SRE-jen, please own the postmortem. Devex-Liz, draft a brief customer-facing blurb for status page.
devex-liz: drafting status update: explain mitigation steps, note potential increased latency for customers routed to eu-central, and mention dedicated customers affected and that they were contacted.

incident-bot: Incident 1923456789 mitigated. Duration ~25m active, moved to monitoring. Root factors: OOM triggered by quantization canary + third-party plugin on customer pinned nodes + transient network resets. Actions: node cordon/drain, emergency failover, model-variant override, cache warm, circuit-breaker, scaling, customer rollback.

oncall-ada: final metrics before handoff:
- peak eu-west1 5xx: 11.8%
- current global 5xx: 0.4%
- failover policy active for non-pinned traffic (eu-central fallback)
- drained node reintroduced after health checks
- postmortem owner: sre-jen

oncall-ada: thanks all. Closing channel in 10m unless new regressions. :white_check_mark:
